cards.text: The LORD is still speaking to Moses, Israel's leader, with words for the Israelites. He opens with no idols. That means no carved image, no sacred pillar, and no sculpted stone set up in the land to bow down to.

cards.question: The LORD forbids the Israelites to make idols and bow down to a sculpted stone. What reason does He give?

answers.text: Because He is the LORD their God
Because the nations will mock them

cards.question: Along with no idols, the LORD tells the Israelites to keep His Sabbaths and have reverence for His sanctuary.

cards.text: Then the LORD lays out an if: 'If you follow My statutes and carefully keep My commandments,' and here's what comes with it.

cards.question: If the Israelites obey, what's the first thing the LORD says He'll give them?

cards.text: The land will yield, the trees will bear fruit, and the threshing will run until the grape harvest, which runs until sowing time. That's my bakery in December, friend: one batch comes out and the timer's already YELLING about the next one.

cards.question: With one harvest running right into the next, the LORD says the Israelites will eat their fill and dwell securely in their land.

cards.text: Then the LORD promises peace in the land. They'll lie down with nothing to fear, and no sword will pass through.

cards.question: Even with peace in the land, the LORD says dangerous animals will still roam it.

cards.text: And when enemies show up? Israel will do the chasing, and the enemies will fall by the sword.

cards.question: The LORD gets specific about the chase. Five Israelites will pursue how many enemies?

cards.text: And a hundred of them will pursue ten thousand. Friend, five of ME couldn't chase a hundred ants off the counter, and I've got a mustache BUILT for sweeping.
The LORD says He'll turn toward them, make them fruitful and multiply them. And He'll establish His covenant with them.

cards.question: The LORD says the Israelites will still be eating the ___ supply of grain when they need to clear it out to make room for the ___ one.
On top of all the blessings in the fields, the LORD says He'll make His dwelling place among the Israelites.

cards.text: And His soul will not despise them. He says, 'I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.'

cards.question: The LORD reminds the Israelites that He brought them out of ___ so they would no longer be slaves.
The LORD says He broke the bars of the Israelites' yoke. What did that enable them to do?

cards.text: Then the sermon flips, friend, and here comes the other if. If they reject His statutes, despise His ordinances and so break His covenant.
The LORD says He'll bring sudden terror, wasting disease, and fever that will destroy their sight and drain their life. Even the seed they sow will be sown in vain.

cards.question: The Israelites will sow their seed in vain, because their ___ will eat it.

cards.text: The LORD says He'll set His face against them, they'll be defeated, and those who hate them will rule over them. That's a hard turn from the blessings, friend.

cards.question: In the blessings, the LORD said Israel would do the chasing. Now what does He say the Israelites will do?

answers.text: Flee when no one pursues them
Hide when no one sees them
Fight when no one leads them

cards.text: And if after all this they still won't obey, the LORD says He'll punish them sevenfold for their sins. And He's not done speaking, friend.

cards.question: Next, the LORD says He'll break something down in the Israelites. What is it?

cards.text: He says He'll make their sky like iron and their land like bronze. Their strength will be spent in vain.

cards.question: With the sky like iron and the land like bronze, the LORD says the land will still yield its produce, just less of it.

cards.text: Then a new word shows up, friend: hostility. If they walk in hostility toward Him and refuse to obey, the LORD says He'll multiply their plagues seven times, according to their sins.

cards.question: In the blessings, the LORD promised to rid the land of dangerous animals. What does He say He'll send against the Israelites now?
The LORD says the wild animals He sends will leave the Israelites' livestock alone.

cards.text: The LORD keeps going, and I'm leaning in here, friend. What if, in spite of these things, they still walk in hostility toward Him?

cards.question: If the Israelites keep walking in hostility toward the LORD, what does He say they won't accept?

cards.text: Now the LORD says, 'then I will act with hostility toward you, and I will strike you sevenfold for your sins.' He'll bring a sword against them to execute the vengeance of the covenant.

cards.question: Even if the Israelites withdraw into their cities, the LORD says He'll send a ___ among them.

cards.text: When the LORD cuts off their supply of bread, ten women will bake bread in a single oven and dole it out by weight. I've got warm ovens all over my bakery, friend, and I can't picture TEN people crowded around just one.

cards.question: With bread doled out by weight, the LORD says the Israelites will eat but not be satisfied.

cards.text: Then the LORD goes further, and I think this is the hardest part to hear. If they still don't obey, the LORD says He'll walk in fury against them and punish them sevenfold, and they'll eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters.
He'll destroy their high places and cut down their incense altars. He'll heap their lifeless bodies on the lifeless remains of their idols.

cards.question: In the blessings, the LORD said His soul would not despise the Israelites. What does He say now?

answers.text: His soul will wait for them

cards.question: As their cities are reduced to rubble, the LORD says He'll still accept the pleasing aroma of the Israelites' sacrifices.

cards.text: He'll lay waste the land, so that the enemies who dwell in it will be appalled. And He'll scatter Israel among the nations.

cards.question: With the Israelites gone and the land lying desolate, the LORD says the land will enjoy its ___.
What rest does the land get while it lies desolate?

answers.text: The rest it missed while Israel lived there
The rest its new owners give it
The rest it earned from great harvests

cards.question: The LORD sends faintness into the hearts of the survivors in enemy lands. What will be enough to put them to flight?

answers.text: The sound of a windblown leaf
The cry of a single bird
The shadow of a passing cloud

cards.text: They'll flee as one flees the sword and stumble over one another, though no one is behind them. I think that's a heavy way to live, friend.

cards.question: The LORD says the survivors scattered among the nations will grow strong in the lands of their enemies.

cards.text: But then the LORD says another if. What if they confess their iniquity and their fathers' iniquity, and their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they make amends?

cards.question: If the Israelites confess and their hearts are humbled, what does the LORD say He'll remember?

answers.text: Every one of their past sins

cards.text: He names Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, Israel's forefathers. And He says He'll remember the land too.

cards.question: The LORD says the Israelites will pay the penalty for their iniquity because they turned their backs on His ordinances and statutes.
Once the Israelites are in the land of their enemies, the LORD says He will reject them so as to destroy them and break His covenant with them.

cards.text: For their sake, He'll remember the covenant with their fathers, whom He brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God. And He closes with this: 'I am the LORD.'

cards.question: These are the statutes, ordinances and laws the LORD established with the Israelites through Moses on Mount ___.

cards.text: That's where we'll set this batch down for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this teaching isn't done yet.
